recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and do not widen Reference.identifier for this issue. Any future move to multiple core identifiers would need a new normative-change decision rather than a reconciliation change for FHIR-30878.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification Jira requested relaxing Reference.identifier from 0..1 to 0..* so logical references could carry multiple known business identifiers. The accepted resolution rejected a direct max-cardinality change because Reference is normative and instead required a standard additionalIdentifier extension plus Reference.identifier usage-note guidance.
initial_application: Git commit 0bdbd05b41b1a83334cde1e26cfb7d30a59b6e72 appears to have applied the issue by adding additionalIdentifier to the Reference datatype extensions spreadsheet and adding Reference.identifier comment text that directs additional identifiers to the extension. Later core source removed datatype extension definitions from the FHIR core checkout; the additionalIdentifier StructureDefinition now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread documents the exact implementer use case and the concern that Reference.identifier is normative. FHIR-I minutes show the work group considered a Reference.additionalIdentifiers/core extension path, voted FHIR-30878 Persuasive with Modification, and later voted FHIR-36212 as a duplicate of FHIR-30878. Current source/fhir.ini keeps Reference as an active normative datatype, source/datatypes/reference.xml keeps Reference.identifier at 0..1 with additionalIdentifier guidance, and the Extension Pack defines additionalIdentifier for Reference with max * Identifier values.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source hunk is needed because the current build-scope source and external Extension Pack definition already express the final FHIR-30878 resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later issue requesting the same Reference.identifier cardinality relaxation was resolved as a duplicate of FHIR-30878 and is already represented on the combined branch.
